memos.headline: S02 and S07 Lead on Trend; S04 in Structural Downtrend; Broad 4-Week Pullback Creates Mixed Signals
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe today. S02 is the standout leader—up 43.7% over 12 weeks with relative strength vs SPY of +31.5% over the same period, sitting just 1.1% off its 52-week high with RSI at 67.9, extended but not yet overbought enough to fade. S07 is similarly powerful on a trend basis (+52% over 26 weeks, +38% above its 200d mean), though the parabolic extension and 3.91% ATR warrant tighter risk management. On the weak side, S04 is in a clear structural downtrend: -27.9% from its 52-week high, trading 13.9% below its 200d mean with negative relative strength across all timeframes—this is a name to avoid until it reclaims its 50d mean. Several names (S03, S05, S10) have pulled back sharply over 4 weeks (-10% to -13%) from otherwise positive 12-week trends; I'd wait for RSI to stabilize above 45 and price to reclaim the 50d mean before getting involved. S06 is quietly constructive with the lowest ATR in the group (2.04%), positive 4-week relative strength, and only a 4.2% drawdown from highs.

views.note: Dominant relative strength (+31.5% vs SPY over 12w), near 52w highs, trend intact—would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~$364).
Massive 12w and 26w momentum with +19.1% relative strength vs SPY, but +38% above 200d mean is parabolic; a break below 880 would shift me neutral.
Steady uptrend with low volatility (ATR 2.04%), +7.8% 4w relative strength vs SPY, RSI 64.9 healthy; would exit on a close below 308.
Structural downtrend: -27.9% from highs, -13.9% below 200d mean, RSI 37.1, negative relative strength on every timeframe—no reason to step in front of this.
RSI 34.8 is the lowest in the universe, -6.4% below 50d mean, 4w relative strength -9.9% vs SPY; needs to reclaim 254 (50d area) to turn constructive.
Above both moving averages but sharp -5.3% weekly drop and fading RSI at 44; watching 283 (50d mean area) as support—break below flips to avoid.
Positive 4w relative strength (+5.7%) but only +0.4% above 200d mean and -10.5% from highs; trend is flat, not compelling either way.
Strong 12w trend (+16.9%) but violent 4w pullback of -10.3% and -9.5% relative strength vs SPY; need to see RSI recover above 50 before committing.
Flat on the week after a -13% 4w drawdown with highest ATR in the group (4.06%); too volatile and unclear near-term to have conviction.
12w relative strength vs SPY is -18.9%, the worst in the universe; despite +25.5% 26w return, the trend has clearly rolled over with RSI at 43.3.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Faces Margin Collapse
memos.body: I am most convicted on the divergence between the high-margin growers and the names showing cash-flow compression. S10 posted 85.2% YoY revenue growth to $81.6B with a staggering 71.5% net margin and only $8.5B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings profile in the universe. S05 delivered $62.6B of net income on $109.9B of revenue (56.9% margin) with net income up 81.2% YoY and minimal leverage at $14.8B of debt, which is durable and capital-light. On the other end, S09 printed just 4.9% net margin on $85.1B of revenue with net income down 45.8% YoY, and S02 grew revenue only 2.0% with a thin 5.6% margin and flat earnings — neither name earns its cost of capital at these margins. I would need to see S09 stabilize net income and S02 show operating leverage before reconsidering; conversely, any deceleration in S10's top-line growth or margin compression below 60% would prompt a downgrade.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and negligible $8.5B debt make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 81% YoY net income growth and only $14.8B debt signals durable, capital-light earnings power.
38.3% net margin, 23% net income growth, and moderate $40.3B debt represent solid high-quality compounding.
Revenue of $181.5B and 76.7% net income growth are impressive, but 16.7% margin and $122.6B of debt leave less room for error.
Solid 26.6% margin and 16.6% revenue growth, but $82.7B of total debt warrants monitoring leverage trends.
22% revenue growth is encouraging but 14.6% margin and $36.2B debt on $17.4B revenue imply high leverage relative to earnings.
33.1% margin is healthy but $448.8B of total debt dwarfs revenue; earnings growth of 12.6% is the slowest among profitable names.
18.5% margin is decent but 7.4% revenue growth and only 4.3% net income growth suggest limited upside catalyst.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin — clear cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Only 2% revenue growth, 5.6% net margin, and flat net income with $77.9B debt signal no durable earnings power at current levels.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates — Favor Defensives Over Duration
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months, down 75bp over the past year, but the easing cycle appears stalled with headline CPI running at 3.8% YoY and 1.8% over just the last three months (annualizing above 7%). The labor market is stable — unemployment at 4.30%, down 10bp over three months and flat YoY — giving the Fed no urgency to cut further. Meanwhile, the 10y yield has risen 21bp over three months to 4.48%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 17bp to just 0.40pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and potentially tighter financial conditions ahead. This regime — paused policy, sticky inflation, rising long-end yields — is unfavorable for duration-sensitive growth and constructive for banks and staples. A CPI print showing YoY inflation falling below 3% or unemployment spiking above 4.6% would change my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds as 10y yields rise 21bp over 3 months with no near-term rate cuts in sight.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (10y-2y at +0.40pp) and stable employment supporting credit quality, though spread compression bears watching.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a sticky-inflation, higher-for-longer rate environment with stable labor markets.
Cyclicals face mixed signals — stable employment is supportive but rising long rates and sticky inflation could weigh on consumer spending.
Energy is less rate-sensitive but the macro backdrop of paused easing and no clear growth acceleration leaves me without strong conviction.
High-duration growth names are vulnerable as the 10y yield grinds higher and the Fed shows no inclination to resume cutting with CPI at 3.8% YoY.

memos.headline: Earnings-Season Sentiment Divergence: S05, S07, S02 Positive Momentum vs. S04, S10 Negative Drift
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence as proxies for sentiment direction across the universe. S05 (+10.0%), S07 (+9.9%), and S02 (+7.0%) all posted strong positive reactions to their Q1 results, and S05 in particular has sustained a high volume of material filings through early June—including new definitive agreements and bylaw amendments—suggesting an active corporate narrative that should keep sentiment elevated. On the negative side, S04 saw a -3.9% earnings-day reaction followed by two director departure/appointment filings, which I read as management instability layered on top of already sour tone; S10 similarly posted -1.8% on its May 20 results and has had two separate officer-change filings, reinforcing a negative narrative. S08 (+3.2%) and S01 (+1.7%) had mildly positive earnings reactions but lack follow-through catalysts, so I treat their sentiment as largely priced. I have highest conviction on S05 and S04 where the filing volume and price signals align directionally, and lower conviction elsewhere where the signal is thinner.

views.note: Strongest earnings reaction at +10.0% combined with an unusually dense stream of material agreements and governance filings through June suggests a positive narrative shift still unfolding.
A +9.9% earnings-day pop and fresh Reg FD disclosure on June 11 indicate management is actively guiding sentiment higher, though filing volume is lighter than S05.
The +7.0% earnings reaction was the second-strongest in the universe and the May Reg FD filing keeps the communication channel open, but no material catalysts since then tempers conviction.
Negative -3.9% earnings reaction followed by two director departure/appointment filings signals management churn on top of weak fundamentals—sentiment trajectory is clearly negative.
Two officer-change 8-Ks preceding a -1.8% earnings reaction paint a picture of organizational disruption and tepid results; sentiment is drifting lower.
Mild +3.2% earnings pop is constructive but the officer-change filing and absence of follow-through catalysts suggest the positive tone is already priced.
Muted +0.8% earnings reaction and a new debt obligation filed June 10 create an ambiguous sentiment picture—not clearly positive or negative.
A modest +1.7% Q3 earnings reaction and Reg FD disclosure are mildly positive but lack the magnitude or follow-through to signal a narrative shift.
Slight -1.0% earnings reaction and a subsequent officer change are marginally negative but too small to build conviction either way.
High filing volume (six 8-Ks) but no earnings reaction data and mostly governance/other-events filings make it hard to read directional sentiment.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Falling Fast but Elevated Oil and Rising VIX Signal Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped sharply—down 39% over three months to 257—but remains well above historical norms, suggesting that while the worst policy shock (likely tariff/sanctions-related) is fading, structural uncertainty persists. WTI at $91.58 is up 5.5% over three months even as it pulled back nearly 10% in the last month, consistent with an energy supply environment still under geopolitical stress (sanctions enforcement, OPEC+ dynamics). The VIX ticking up 5.8% month-over-month to 19.44 while HY spreads stay tight at 2.78% tells me credit markets are sanguine but equity vol is pricing in near-term event risk—possibly around trade policy or export controls. S06 has filed four 8-Ks in under two months (all 8.01 Other Events), which in a geopolitical context could reflect supply-chain or regulatory disclosures worth monitoring. I have moderate conviction that energy-exposed and policy-sensitive names face asymmetric downside if sanctions or export controls tighten, while the broad de-escalation in uncertainty supports names with less geopolitical surface area.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K cadence (four filings in ~6 weeks) warrants caution until content is clarified; could reflect regulatory or supply-chain adjustments tied to policy shifts.

Three 8-Ks in a month including both Reg FD and Other Events suggest active disclosure posture; with policy uncertainty still elevated I stay neutral pending clarity on whether filings relate to geopolitical exposure.
Two Reg FD filings (April and just yesterday) amid falling policy uncertainty and tight credit spreads suggest proactive investor engagement in a more benign policy backdrop; lean constructive.
Single Reg FD filing in late April with no follow-up; insufficient geopolitical signal to take a directional view.
One Reg FD filing in early May; no evidence of outsized geopolitical exposure but oil at $91.58 and residual policy uncertainty keep me sidelined.
Falling policy uncertainty (down 39% over 3 months) and tight HY spreads favor names with limited geopolitical tail risk; single Reg FD filing is benign.
